commits.subject: Name Ultra-Regular as the release does
commits.body:
The release's names differ from what FontForge exported from this file;
it states them as US English names: ID 4 'Ultra Regular' (FontForge exported 'Ultra'); ID 6 'Ultra-Regular' (FontForge exported 'Ultra').

commits.subject: Class the combining marks as marks, as shapers treat them in the release
commits.body: The release was exported without OpenType layout: it has a legacy kern table and no GDEF, so shapers class its glyphs by Unicode category and treat these 3 combining marks (category Mn) as marks, giving them no advance after a base. This file leaves them automatic, which classes a glyph without anchors as a base. Stating GlyphClass 4 (mark) keeps the shaping the release has. Glyph list: every glyph the release (google/fonts apache/ultra/Ultra-Regular.ttf) maps to a Unicode Mn code point.

disclose: The released font has only a legacy `kern` table and no GPOS. fontc writes kerning as GPOS, and a font with GPOS no longer gets HarfBuzz's built-in placement of combining marks, so combining marks are positioned differently from the release (e.g. U+0312, U+0326, U+0315). Decided 2026-10-01: accept and disclose.

The build has a GDEF table where the release (legacy kern table only) has none: it classes the combining marks as marks, as shapers already treated them in the release, and fontc's kerning lookup skips those marks through a mark filtering set, because fontc's kerning writer always skips marks (the release's kern table kerns every pair). Shaping differs from the release in exactly the runs the legacy-kern difference already accounts for. Needs a fontc change (KernFeatureWriter ignoreMarks); planned as later work. Decided 2026-10-02: disclose.
